attribution.note: These are Zitron's own words on his own blog, giving his own estimate.

semantics.note: The claim keeps 'I see', 'around $22 billion', the global scope, the exclusion of OpenAI and Anthropic, and the indeterminate startup share. No period or basis is stated, and the claim adds none.

contract.note: The contract correctly finds no period, basis or method. Any test would need a framing the speaker did not supply, so leaving it unscored is fair.

attribution.note: This is Zitron's own reasoning in his post, stated in his own voice.

semantics.note: The chain is stated flatly with 'will', and the antecedent 'if one customer can't pay' is kept. It has no deadline.

contract.note: Reading 'customer' as a data-center tenant whose payments back the debt fits the context, which is about data-center bond collateral. The test for the antecedent is reasonable.

evidence.note: A dated tracker from before the evaluation date. It finds no neocloud default and no data-center tenant failing to pay, which shows the antecedent had not occurred. It says nothing about the outcome of the chain.

reviews.rationale: This is an open-ended conditional forecast. The packet shows no AI data-center tenant failing to pay by the cutoff, so the antecedent has not happened and the chain cannot be scored yet.

attribution.note: These are Zitron's own words, restating his earlier argument as his own view.

semantics.note: The causal chain is kept: high valuations and repeated rounds push valuations so high that an IPO or acquisition becomes 'impossible'. 'Devil's deal' is the evaluative framing around that chain.

contract.note: The plain reading treats 'impossible' as 'cannot as a rule', which is if anything generous to him. The 2026 window up to the post date is a reasonable reading of his present-tense claim.

evidence.note: SpaceX agreed to buy Cursor, a venture-backed AI startup, for $60B, about twice its $29.3B last private valuation.
The Cursor acquisition closed in August 2026, before the post.

Several multi-billion-dollar AI startup deals were agreed or closed in Aug–Sep 2026: Hugging Face, Poolside and OpenRouter. These are weaker evidence, since prior valuations are not given and Hugging Face had not closed.
The Cerebras IPO was large, but Cerebras was a profitable hardware maker, so it falls outside his 'IP-light, EBITDA-negative' class.

reviews.rationale: In the period he describes, a heavily funded AI startup was acquired at about twice its last private valuation and the deal closed (Cursor), and several other multi-billion-dollar AI startup deals followed. This contradicts the claim that such exits are 'impossible', even read as 'as a rule'. Cursor's EBITDA is not confirmed in the packet, but the counterexamples are enough.
